parts.label: a.i
parts.display_text: A spectral line has wavelength 434 nm for a stationary source and is observed at 502 nm from a receding astronomical source. State whether this is a redshift or a blueshift, and what the shift indicates about radial motion.

answer.text: It is a redshift: the observed wavelength is longer. In the Doppler interpretation, the source is receding from the observer.

bridge_result.text: It is a redshift: the observed wavelength is longer. In the Doppler interpretation, the source is receding from the observer.

answer.text: Official answer A; editorial worked explanation: An approaching source produces a frequency above f₀. As the source slows, the observed frequency moves back toward f₀; when the source reaches rest at T, the fractional shift is zero. Only graph A starts positive and falls to zero.
answer.evidence: Official May 2025 Physics SL Paper 1A TZ1 markscheme 2225-6710M, PDF page 3; editorial explanation independently checked against the original source.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
A star emits a spectral line with a known rest wavelength. The star is moving away from Earth. Compared with the rest values, how do the wavelength and frequency received on Earth change?

A. Both increase
B. Wavelength increases; frequency decreases
C. Wavelength decreases; frequency increases
D. Both decrease

answer.text: B. Recession produces redshift: received wavelength increases. Since light still travels at c, its received frequency decreases.

evidence.review: Derived independently from the question and checked against the first-assessment2025 IB Physics guide; handwritten annotations are not answer evidence.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
A toy drone moves counterclockwise at constant speed around the horizontal circle shown. A stationary microphone lies just beyond point W. The drone emits a constant frequency. From which part of its path is the sound with the highest received frequency emitted?

A. At Z
B. At X
C. Between Y and Z
D. Between Z and W

answer.text: D. The approach component is greatest where the velocity is directed along the tangent toward the microphone. That tangent point is between Z and W.

evidence.review: Derived independently from the question and checked against the first-assessment2025 IB Physics guide; handwritten annotations are not answer evidence.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
A truck travels east at 25 m s⁻¹ while sounding a constant-frequency horn. A is behind it moving east at 10 m s⁻¹; B is ahead moving west at 10 m s⁻¹; C is stationary behind it; D is stationary ahead of it. Which observer hears the highest frequency?

A. A
B. B
C. C
D. D

answer.text: B. The wavefronts are compressed ahead of the truck. Observer B also moves towards those arriving wavefronts, receiving them more frequently than stationary D.

evidence.review: Checked source answer/scoring guide and independently worked adapted version.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
A car moves at constant speed in a straight line away from stationary listener P and towards stationary listener Q, remaining between them throughout. Its horn emits a constant frequency. Which statements are correct?

1. P hears an increasing frequency.
2. Q hears a decreasing frequency.
3. Q hears a higher frequency than P.

A. 1, 2 and 3
B. 1 and 2 only
C. 3 only
D. None

answer.text: C. Both observed frequencies stay constant because the source velocities towards or away from the listeners are constant. Q hears a higher frequency, and P a lower frequency, than the emitted frequency; only statement 3 is correct.

evidence.review: Source question, official answer and adapted solution checked individually.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: At the opposite edge of the rotating Sun, the surface moves towards the observer. How does the observed wavelength of a spectral line compare with its emitted wavelength? Explain.

answer.text: The observed wavelength is shorter: the approaching source produces a blueshift, with successive wavefronts reaching the observer closer together.

evidence.review: Source question, official answer and adapted solution checked individually.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
A child swings past a stationary man while blowing a constant-frequency whistle. At which position is the heard frequency highest?

A. At X
B. At Y moving away
C. At Y moving toward the man
D. At Z

answer.text:
Official key C checked; editorial worked explanation:

C. Doppler frequency is greatest when the source approaches with the largest velocity component toward the observer. The swing’s speed is greatest at the lowest point Y, and the approaching pass therefore gives the highest frequency.

evidence.detail: Cambridge 9702/12 May/June 2024 published key C, PDF page 2; explanation is editorial.

source.syllabus: Cambridge International AS & A Level Physics 9702

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
An observer hears a moving sound source at a frequency lower than the emitted frequency. What could cause this?

A. The source moves away.
B. The source moves toward.
C. Sound speed decreases because the source moves.
D. Sound speed increases because the source moves.

answer.text:
Published key A checked; editorial worked explanation:

A. A source moving away leaves successive wavefronts farther apart in the observer’s direction, increasing wavelength and lowering the observed frequency. The speed of sound is set by the medium and is not changed by the source motion.

evidence.detail: Cambridge 9702/12 February/March 2023 published key A, PDF page 2; explanation independently authored and checked.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
The Doppler effect can be observed

A. only in sound waves.
B. in all mechanical waves.
C. only in electromagnetic waves.
D. in water waves and sound waves but not in electromagnetic waves.

answer.text: Official key B checked; editorial worked explanation: all mechanical waves can show Doppler shifts. Electromagnetic waves can too, so exclusivity claims are false.

evidence.detail: Official VCAA 2022 NHT report checked for Section A Question 15; explanation is editorial.

ibd-56ec7b86c6b34d97-q16:whole.hint: Use the sign of the shift for an approaching source, then apply the endpoint condition when the source stops.
notes: An approaching source compresses the wavefront spacing in front of it, so the observer receives a frequency above f₀.
The qualitative sign and endpoint are sufficient: the shift must vanish when the source is stationary at T.

original-ib26mb1a-mcq-11:whole.hint: Consider how successive wavefronts are spaced when a source moves away, then use c=fλ.
notes: Redshift describes an increase in wavelength of an identifiable spectral feature, not a claim that every star appears red.
For electromagnetic waves in vacuum the wave speed remains c. A wavelength change is accompanied by the opposite frequency change.

original-ib26mb1a-mcq-23:whole.hint: Draw a tangent for the drone’s velocity and compare its component along the line to the microphone.
notes: Doppler shift depends on the component of relative velocity along the source–observer line, not simply on which point is nearest the microphone.
The question specifies the position when sound is emitted. The drone continues moving while the sound travels to the microphone.

cross-ca24m1-26:whole.hint: Decide whether the source is moving towards or away from the observer along their line of sight.
notes: Approach compresses the arriving wavefronts and raises the observed frequency; recession spreads them and lowers it. The source frequency stays unchanged.
For a source passing to one side of an observer, consider the component of motion along the source–observer line. This question needs qualitative reasoning, not the higher-level Doppler formula.
